newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Year-end profittaking weighs on Belgian bonds.
newsitem.headline: Year-end profittaking weighs on Belgian bonds.

text.p: A light but persistant trickle of profittaking selling weighed on Belgian linear bonds on Tuesday in what traders said could remain the trend at least until the New Year when they expected a stronger sell-off.
"It was a day of profittaking selling," one trader said. "There was business all along the curve."
"People expect a real sell-off at the start of the New Year, so they are becoming very cautious," another said.
However, traders said that while the actual volume of business on Tuesday was fair in relation to recent days, it was still quite small.

Traders said they expected end investors, who have held back from selling before the New Year for fear of being hit by heavy capital gains taxes, to start offloading with a vengeance at the start of January.
However, if the U.S. market started moving down seriously, these end investors could be stampeded into selling earlier, traders said.
"Everyone is watching everyone else in this market. As soon as one sells they will all follow," one trader said. "In this race the first to move is the real winner."
The yield of the benchmark 2006 OLO edged up to 5.99 percent from Monday's 5.96, and the spread over German Bunds narrowed to nine basis points from 11.
The December futures contract was 23 basis points down at 120.68, having moved in a 120.85/120.59 range.
